gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 22?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 22 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent official forecasts from Deutscher Wetterdienst-influenced models and international ensembles project a Munich high of 20–21°C on August 22 under weak westerly flow, partly cloudy skies, and light winds of 10–12 mph. These conditions limit daytime heating and align with the market's leading implied probabilities of 40.5% for 21°C and 30% for 20°C. Ensemble consensus and historical August climatology support this narrow range, though minor shifts in cloud cover or wind could push the actual maximum toward 22°C. Traders are weighting the latest model runs heavily ahead of tomorrow's official observation.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader consensus has coalesced around an official daily maximum of 79°F at Central Park, the primary NWS station for NYC temperature records.**  

The National Weather Service climate summary for August 21, 2026, recorded a high of 79°F at 2:59 PM under mostly cloudy skies with light northeast winds and trace precipitation, placing the value squarely in the 78-79°F bin. This outcome sits 4°F below the 1991–2020 normal high of 83°F, consistent with regional observations of onshore flow and persistent cloud cover that limited daytime heating. Multiple automated reports from nearby sites (e.g., Newark and LaGuardia) aligned closely, reinforcing the Central Park reading as the authoritative benchmark for market resolution.  

The near-100% implied probability reflects the high reliability of these verified, quality-controlled observations, which have minimal revision risk once finalized. The only realistic scenarios that could shift resolution involve an unforeseen post-publication data correction at the station or an atypical market rule using a non-standard sensor—both low-probability events given standard NWS protocols. Historical context shows August 21 highs typically range from the mid-70s to low-80s, making the observed value typical rather than anomalous.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts and ensemble models for August 23 point to a Tokyo high near 31°C, the main driver behind the near-even 36% and 32.5% market-implied odds on 30°C and 31°C. Persistent strengthening of the Pacific High has sustained above-normal temperatures across Honshu this summer, with historical August averages of 30.6°C serving as the baseline. Key differentiating factors include urban heat island effects that can add 1–2°C in central districts, variable cloud cover and shower chances that limit daytime heating, and minor model spread in boundary-layer moisture. Resolution hinges on official JMA observations at the Tokyo station, with any late-day sea-breeze shift or thicker cloud deck the most likely variables that could tip the outcome between the two leading bins.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest numerical weather prediction consensus from the ECMWF, GFS, and DWD points to a Munich maximum near 21–23°C on August 23 under mostly clear skies, light winds, and stable high pressure that favors modest daytime heating without significant advection or cloud cover. eventMetadata.context_description: Recent official forecasts position 23–24°C as the leading outcomes for Munich’s daily maximum on August 24, reflecting post-frontal stabilization and modest daytime heating under partly cloudy skies with westerly flow. A recent cold front has advected cooler maritime air, keeping values near or slightly below the late-August climatological mean of roughly 23°C, while ensemble guidance from European and global models shows limited spread around 22–25°C. Low precipitation probability and modest diurnal ranges further constrain upside risk, though variable cloud cover or brief clearing could nudge the peak toward 25°C. Trader probabilities align closely with this narrow forecast envelope ahead of official Deutscher Wetterdienst observations.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official National Weather Service guidance and ensemble model consensus point to a daily maximum near 77°F in New York City today under mostly cloudy skies with showers likely and northeast winds at 5–10 mph, directly supporting the market’s leading 76–77°F outcome at 45.5% implied probability. Persistent marine-layer influence and onshore flow have suppressed temperatures several degrees below the late-August climatological average of roughly 82°F, while limited afternoon destabilization reduces the odds of brief warming into the upper 70s. Recent observational trends and updated short-range guidance have tightened the distribution around the mid-70s, explaining the combined 71.5% probability assigned to the 74–79°F bins and the minimal pricing below 72°F or above 80°F.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent numerical weather prediction ensembles from the Deutscher Wetterdienst and ECMWF project a mostly sunny regime over southern Germany on August 24, with modest insolation and light westerly flow supporting daytime maxima centered on 22–24 °C—slightly below the late-August climatological mean of ~23.7 °C. A preceding frontal passage has advected cooler, drier air that limits boundary-layer heating while suppressing cloud build-up, producing the tight 22–25 °C cluster reflected in market-implied odds. Remaining spread among outcomes arises from modest uncertainties in cloud timing, surface wind mixing, and local urban heat-island effects, all of which can shift the recorded maximum by 1–2 °C within the final 48-hour forecast window.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 23 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service forecasts for New York City on August 23 indicate a daytime high near 82°F under partly cloudy skies with a 40-60% chance of showers and thunderstorms, primarily in the afternoon. This positions the 80-81°F and 82-83°F bins as near-even market leaders, reflecting traders' weighting of forecast spread across models. Key differentiators include the timing and coverage of convective clouds, which can cap peak temperatures by reducing insolation, versus clearer southwest flow that allows readings to reach the mid-80s. Easterly morning winds shifting southwest, combined with high humidity, add modest uncertainty to maximum values, while historical August averages near 82°F provide context for the tight distribution. Updated model runs and evening observations will likely refine these implied probabilities ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecasts and midday observations position 21°C as the leading outcome for Munich's August 22 high.** Persistent westerly flow and partial cloud cover have limited daytime heating, with temperatures reaching only about 19°C by early afternoon under mostly cloudy skies and moderate winds around 18–20 km/h. Multiple models, including GFS-based guidance, converge on a peak near 20–21°C (68–70°F), slightly below the long-term August average high of ~23°C. Light showers or virga in some runs further suppress maxima, reducing odds of 22°C or higher while making sub-20°C readings unlikely given the current trajectory. Traders assign 72.5% implied probability to 21°C because official station data and short-range forecasts show little scope for significant warming before sunset.

eventMetadata.context_description: Traders are aligning closely on 22–23°C as the August 23 high in Munich because short-range ensemble forecasts from the ECMWF and German Weather Service converge on that narrow band under a strengthening high-pressure ridge. eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent official forecasts position 23–25°C as the most likely range for Munich’s maximum temperature on August 24, 2026, aligning closely with the market’s leading outcomes (24°C at 36%, 23°C at 26%, 25°C at 20%).**  

European and global models, including runs referenced by the German Weather Service and Met Office, indicate a transitional late-summer pattern under building high pressure, with daytime maxima stabilizing in the low-to-mid 20s °C after cooler conditions on the 22nd–23rd. Historical August averages for Munich hover near 23°C, and the current setup lacks the strong southerly flow or clear-sky radiative heating that produced the 31°C spike earlier in the month.  

Short-range model consensus shows limited day-to-day variability for the 24th, with light easterly winds and scattered cloud reducing the chance of extremes above 26°C or below 22°C. Traders appear to weight the latest deterministic and ensemble guidance heavily, as resolution is imminent and further model updates will have diminishing impact before the daily high is recorded.

Updated model runs over the next 48 hours will refine these temperature thresholds ahead of market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and ensemble forecasts indicate above-normal temperatures for late August 2026, with Tokyo's urban heat island and persistent high humidity supporting daytime maxima clustered around 31–33 °C. Model consensus for August 24 points to partly cloudy conditions with isolated showers that could cap the peak near 32 °C while limiting stronger radiative heating. Historical climatology shows typical late-August highs of 31–32 °C, yet the current season's elevated baseline—following record 2025 warmth—shifts probabilities toward the upper end of that range. Traders appear to weigh these short-range model runs against potential timing shifts in frontal boundaries or localized convection when pricing the 32 °C and 33 °C bins as the clearest outcomes ahead of final observational data.

Moderate winds of 15–20 km/h and scattered light showers or virga further suppress surface temperatures, keeping peaks 2–3°C below the long-term August average high of roughly 23–24°C. Traders view 22°C as plausible only with rapid clearing before sunset, while sub-20°C or 23°C+ readings remain low-probability given the stable synoptic pattern and limited remaining insolation. Updated forecast runs and final station data tonight will confirm resolution.

These conditions match the long-term August 24 climatological average high of 23.4°C and recent model consensus showing no heatwave setup or anomalous warmth.

Recent data as of August 22 show consistent guidance across sources with no significant forecast shifts in the past 24–48 hours. Low precipitation probabilities (near 5%) and moderate humidity further support contained daytime maxima, keeping extreme outcomes like 28°C+ at just 2% implied probability. Updated model runs or any unexpected clearing could nudge values slightly higher within the 23–25°C range, but current evidence points to stable, near-normal late-summer conditions.
